card.intuition: One user message plus everything the agent does in response, up until it yields back to the user. A turn contains one or more model provider requests — many if the agent calls tools. The hierarchy is session > turn > model provider request, and turn length is the agent's decision, not yours.
card.analogy: Delegating one item to a teammate who then makes several follow-up calls and checks before reporting back: you handed over a single request, but the teammate decided how much internal work to chain before yielding.
card.time_complexity: The model re-reads the entire context on every turn, so cost and latency grow with context size per request.
card.space_complexity: Each turn appends its messages and tool results to the session, consuming context-window budget until compaction or clearing.
when_to_use: Steering between turns, where the agent yields back and you can redirect
Asking for smaller turns — a plan first, one step at a time — to trade autonomy for control
Interrupting a long turn in a harness that supports mid-turn steering
gotchas: Long turns are where things go wrong unsupervised — by the time the agent yields it may have drifted far from what you meant
A turn with many tool calls is many model provider requests, so latency stacks before the agent ever yields

steps.label: You message
steps.annotation: You hand over one message; the turn opens.

steps.label: Plan
steps.annotation: The agent decides how many steps to chain before yielding back.

steps.label: Tool calls
steps.annotation: Each tool call is a separate model provider request within the turn.

steps.label: Yield
steps.annotation: The agent yields back to you; your reply opens the next turn.

steps.label: Redirect
steps.annotation: Gaps between turns are where you steer and correct direction.

exercise.prompt: Count how many model provider requests happened inside one agent turn, given a transcript of labeled steps.
hints: Every tool call inside a turn is its own model provider request.
Count only the steps whose label begins with model_request:.
exercise.test_code:
steps = ["user: check tests", "model_request:1", "tool: run_tests", "model_request:2", "yield"]
assert count_requests(steps) == 2
assert count_requests(["user: hi", "yield"]) == 0
print('PASS')
